subject: Large Magellanic Cloud
hook: LARGE MAGELLANIC CLOUD IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The Large Magellanic Cloud contains the second-closest supermassive black hole to Earth, which has ejected 21 'hypervelocity stars' that are now traveling through our own Milky Way galaxy.
angle_support: strong evidence for a supermassive black hole in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the second-closest besides Sagittarius A*
21 hypervelocity stars have been discovered within the Milky Way's halo, which are thought to have been ejected from the Large Magellanic Cloud after gravitational interaction with this black hole
title: The LMC hides the Milky Way’s second‑closest supermassive black hole
description: Astronomers have found a supermassive black hole inside the dwarf galaxy Large Magellanic Cloud. Its gravity has flung twenty‑one hypervelocity stars into our Milky Way, making it the second‑closest such monster after Sagittarius A*.
narration: LARGE MAGELLANIC CLOUD IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture supermassive black holes only in huge galaxies like the Milky Way or Andromeda, It’s a dwarf satellite, the Large Magellanic Cloud, that harbors the second‑closest one. Measurements in March 2025 identified a black hole in the LMC weighing about 630,000 solar masses (± 370,000). Twenty‑one hypervelocity stars in our halo trace back to that object via the Hills mechanism, moving faster than 500 km/s. That dwarf galaxy shoots stars across our MilkyWay at breakneck speeds
